provenance.l: MHI — H-IIA launch service, past missions
JAXA — H-IIA F15 (IBUKI, a 202) launch sequence: SECO 15:11, IBUKI separation 16:01, the payload separation delay 50 s (F14: 51 s)

JAXA — H-IIA brochure 2025, H2A202 flight sequence example: SRB-A burnout 97 s, separation 107 s (burnout = chamber pressure at 10 % of maximum); SRB-A burn time 120 s, vacuum Isp 281 s. The SRB-A burns its propellant evenly over the 97 s (no sourced thrust-time curve); flights pick a short- or long-burn variant (F37 92 / 106 s, F40 111 / 127 s, F15 116 / 126 s, JAXA flight sequences); fairing 250 s, MECO 396 s, first / second stage separation 404 s (8 s after MECO, also on F14 and F15)
JAXA — H-IIA F37 and F40 launch sequences (速報): SRB-A burnout 1:32 / 1:51, separation 1:46 / 2:07

Payload 3,020 kg: Kaguya's launch mass (about 3 t; Orrery mission record kaguya, after Kato et al., Space Science Reviews 2010), the heaviest H-IIA payload Orrery flies (Hayabusa2, Akatsuki, Hope, SLIM are lighter); was an unsourced 8,000 kg
